name: Kohala Bridge (Jhelum River)
assumptions: Pier positions come from side-on photos scaled to the OSM length, so each is good to a few metres.
Span layout is modelled symmetric; the second pier at the far bank is seen clearly in only one photo, partly hidden by trees in the others.
Deck width 10.6 m is an estimate from two lanes; no published width was found.
Girder depth, pier plan and parapet height are estimated by eye from photos.
Box girder section comes from the Wikipedia list of bridges; the inside was not seen and is not modelled.
Deck levels come from public terrain at the hillside ends and the photos; no published height exists.
Colours are estimated by eye from photos in mixed light.
Hazard band stripe length of 1.2 m is an estimate from a low resolution aerial photo.
Lamp poles are plain shafts on one side at even spacing; their side, spacing and heads could not be confirmed.
Plinths are given to both river piers; the far one is only partly visible in the photos.
suppress is empty on purpose: the footprint is a line over a deep valley and flattening under it would cut the valley sides.
No night lighting is modelled because no source describes it.
